source: Framland_Protection GitHub README + resume + portfolio + BIOGECKO publication
text: Farmland wildlife intrusion detection (Mar 2023, github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Framland_Protection). An AI-powered, non-lethal alternative to electric fencing and chemical repellents for keeping wildlife off farmland. Pipeline: a camera continuously monitors the farmland; YOLOv3 performs real-time animal detection (about 90% accuracy) with non-maximum suppression to filter redundant boxes; a secondary validation stage (a CNN for species verification plus a Random Forest to filter false positives) cuts false alarms by about 40%; validated detections trigger an Arduino controller that activates non-lethal deterrents matched to the animal type (sound for nocturnal animals, light for herbivores like deer, water sprinklers for medium-sized animals); every detection is logged (image, species, time, location) for conservation and census use. The README's own 'want to improve' section lists upgrading to YOLOv5 as future work - YOLOv3 is what was actually implemented and demoed, though some later materials (the portfolio site's project tag, one resume version) list it as YOLOv5. Won 2nd place among 500+ teams and $300 at the National Technocraft Hackathon (Technocraft Booth Project Competition 2022-23, held at COEP - College of Engineering Pune, 2nd May 2023), and the work was published in BIOGECKO (Vol 12, Issue 03, 2023) on YOLO-based AI detection and automated deterrents. A hardware prototype was built and tested alongside the software pipeline.

Bitcoin price forecasting (2025, Qlik Sense tutorial project under causify-ai/tutorials, TutorTask146). End-to-end pipeline: live BTC price data collection, ARIMA and XGBoost forecasting models achieving around 85% predictive accuracy, automated ingestion/validation/transformation workflows, and interactive Qlik Sense dashboards giving real-time visibility into volatility and market drivers. Cut manual reporting effort by about 40%.

Sage Ventures - multifamily real estate analytics pipeline (2025, github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/RealEstateModelling). A self-built, portfolio demonstration project simulating the data infrastructure, reporting, and BI of a multifamily real estate portfolio (built to demonstrate SQL/Python/Power BI/Excel skills for a Junior Data Analyst-type role; the underlying data is synthetic, generated with the Faker library, not real client data). One-command pipeline (run_pipeline.py) with five phases: generate_data.py builds a SQLite DB and raw CSVs; feature_engineering.py creates 15+ engineered features; adhoc_analysis.py produces 5 business reports; excel_report.py builds a 7-sheet Excel workbook; visualize.py generates 10 automated charts. Data model: properties -> units -> tenants -> rent_roll, plus properties -> maintenance and properties -> occupancy_monthly. Stack: Python, SQLite, SQL, Pandas, openpyxl, Matplotlib, Power BI. Illustrative findings from the simulated portfolio: average occupancy 67% against a 93% target, annual loss-to-lease of $2.14M, $19,864 in current delinquency exposure, and 533 open maintenance tickets past SLA.

CANARIA Anomaly Detection System (github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Version-1-anomaly) - a comprehensive job-market anomaly detection system, closely related to his Canaria Inc. internship work, identifying unusual patterns in job posting data at three granularities: US level (geo_level x source), state level (state x source), and SOC/occupation level (SOC code x source). Pipeline: parquet files are read in configurable batches (default 50,000 rows), cleaned and validated, then stored in MongoDB under a rolling window (configurable, default 45 days) so models keep adapting to recent data without unbounded storage growth. Feature engineering generates 18 engineered features per record: rolling statistics over 7/14/28 days, temporal features (day-of-week, week, month), statistical measures (z-scores, MAD), and expanding-window long-term patterns. The model layer is a 7-model ensemble: PyCaret's Isolation Forest, KNN, and SVM, plus PyOD's HBOS, COPOD, OCSVM, and CBLOF; scores are averaged for robust detection and compared against per-segment, quantile-based thresholds with cooldown logic to prevent alert spam. Output is CSV results with scores plus logging and performance monitoring.

source: Resume_Optimiser GitHub README (this is the outreach-automation project)
text: Resume Optimiser & Outreach Automation (github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Resume_Optimiser) - two tools in one repo, actively developed. (1) A Resume Optimizer CLI (resume_api.py): paste a job description in, get back a tailored one-page LaTeX resume, a cover-letter paragraph, and an email draft, generated via the Claude API and compiled with pdflatex. (2) An Outreach web app (Next.js): upload a contacts CSV, attach a resume, write one email template, preview every personalized message, and send the whole batch through Gmail (OAuth). It also integrates with Apollo.io to search and reveal contacts at a target company (leadership + role-matched tiers) and writes a bespoke, AI-personalized outreach paragraph per contact using Claude Haiku plus a free web-search cascade (Tavily/Exa/Brave) for real context about each person, with guardrails that reject generic-AI-sounding phrasing and casual/unprofessional tone and retry with a correction. Cost and usage are tracked per call (tokens, cache hits, USD) and surfaced in an analytics view.

BudgetPlay (github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/BudgetPlay) - a participatory budgeting simulator built for an Anthropic Hackathon (Track #3: Governance & Accessibility). Lets a user explore how a city-sized budget is allocated, move sliders to rebalance spending across categories, read a Claude-generated plain-language impact narrative explaining the tradeoffs of their reallocation, and optionally submit their proposed budget as a 'vote' grouped by region. A companion 'Government Pulse' dashboard aggregates submissions so community averages can be compared against the official (illustrative, not real) budget, with percentage-point shifts by category and short recommendation blurbs for leaders. Stack: Node.js + Express backend, static frontend (Tailwind, Chart.js, vanilla JS), Anthropic Messages API for the impact-narrative endpoint. The budget data itself is explicitly sample/educational, not an official government budget.

Comparative analysis of RNN architectures for sentiment classification (UMD coursework, github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Sentiment-Analysis). Systematically implements and compares plain RNN, LSTM, and Bidirectional LSTM on the IMDb movie review dataset, varying activation functions (sigmoid, ReLU, tanh), optimizers (Adam, SGD, RMSprop), sequence lengths (25/50/100 words), and gradient clipping on/off, to study how each choice affects sentiment classification performance.

N-gram language modeling and evaluation (UMD coursework, github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/N_Gram_Modelling). Implements and evaluates Maximum Likelihood Estimation n-gram language models (unigram through 4-gram) on the Penn Treebank dataset, studying the trade-offs between n-gram order and the role of smoothing/backoff techniques in handling data sparsity, including perplexity evaluation and text generation.

Comparative analysis of gun violence coverage across news outlets (UMD NLP coursework, github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Comparative_Analysis_HW5). Uses NLP techniques (including coreference resolution via spaCy) to analyze how CNN, Fox News, The New York Times, and The Wall Street Journal portray victims and shooters across gun violence incidents, using a dataset of 100 articles (25 per outlet).
